{{Quote|Don't try to frighten us with your sorcerer's ways, Lord Vader. Your sad devotion to that ancient religion has not helped you conjure up the stolen data tapes, or given you clairvoyance enough to find the Rebels's hidden fort&hellip;|Motti voicing his lack of faith in the force|<ref name="anh" />}}
'''Conan Antonio "Zi" Motti''' was an [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]] who served aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] as the head of [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Naval]] operations during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Born into a [[Motti family|powerful and wealthy family]] on [[Seswenna/Legends|Seswenna]], he entered [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] service, rising rapidly through the ranks of the Imperial Navy. It was not long before he advanced past [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jaim Helaw]], who he had served under early in his career. By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he had been promoted to the rank of [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]], and was working aboard the Empire's massive [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. Only [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] outranked Motti on the battlestation, although [[General/Legends|General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]]&mdash;his counterpart in the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]&mdash;was his equal.

Motti was extremely confident in his viewpoint that the Death Star was invulnerable, believing that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] posed no threat to the [[Space station/Legends|station]]. He was even bold and arrogant enough to openly question [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] for his failure to discover the location of the Rebellion's secret base during one meeting in the [[Death Star conference room/Legends|Death Star conference room]]. For this, Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends#Choking powers|Force-choked]] him, which greatly frightened Motti, who realized that Vader could have easily [[Death/Legends|killed]] him had Tarkin not ordered the Dark Lord to relent. Nonetheless, Motti remained overly confident in himself and the Death Star. Despite Motti's unshakable credence in the Death Star, the Rebel Alliance&mdash;which had obtained a copy of the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star blueprints]]&mdash;managed to find a [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|weak spot]] in the station's defenses, and succeeded in destroying it during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], killing Motti.

==Biography==
===Imperial service===
{{Quote|Motti is ambitious, and he knows this station is his transport to greatness.|Wilhuff Tarkin|<ref name="ds" />}}
[[File:Otto.png|thumb|left|250px|Otto, an Imperial general who Motti was friends with and helped transfer to [[Lok/Legends|Lok]].]]
Hailing from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Seswenna/Legends|Seswenna]],<ref name="I2014" /> Conan Antonio Motti was born into a [[Motti family|powerful and influential family]] several ranks below the [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkin family]] and the rest of the [[Quintad/Legends|Quintad]] sometime during the last years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. As a teenager<ref name="Author's Cut 11">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-11-serving-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 11: Serving the Empire}}</ref> during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], he witnessed the feats of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], memories that would remain with him for his whole life. After the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="ds" /> Motti became an active member of his local Sub-Adult Group for the Seswenna chapter of the Imperial [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]]. He eventually earned an [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Academy]] commission to the planet [[Prefsbelt IV/Legends|Prefsbelt IV]], followed by an appointment to the planet [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]]. While a [[Cadet/Legends|cadet]], Motti was known more for his firebrand [[Politics/Legends|politics]] than academic achievement, though his nature was the typical ruthless Imperial that [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] wished to fill the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] ranks, and he ascended quickly. An [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]] who used force and never apologized for doing so, Motti at some point ended a dispute over the [[Mhalanduin Reformation]] by annihilating the top ranks of both families involved, appointing his own hand-picked [[General/Legends|general]] as a regent. Motti cut a swath through [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] beyond the [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]], and eliminated any who protested the new Imperial authority.<ref name="Author's Cut 11" />

Motti went on to serve aboard the [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class cruiser]] ''[[Ion Storm]]'' under [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jaim Helaw]], who acted as somewhat of a mentor to him, and soon received a promotion to [[First Lieutenant/Legends|first lieutenant]]. Eventually, he worked a brief stint on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], and with the help of contacts he had made on the [[Capital/Legends|capital]], he rose past Helaw.<ref name="ds" /> He was friends with [[Otto]], an Imperial general with several failures on his record, particularly various losses in battle. Motti was able to transfer his friend to an [[Imperial Outpost (Lok)|outpost]] on the planet [[Lok/Legends|Lok]], saving him from the wrath of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].<ref name="galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], Motti was promoted to the rank of [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], during a brief ceremony held on the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']].<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: A New Hope|cardname=One Year Earlier: Admiral Motti}}</ref> In the same year, Motti, alongside [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arhul Kurumenga]] of the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]] and [[Master of Imperial Projects]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]], attended a debriefing on Coruscant helmed by Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]], a [[Pre-Republic era|Pre-Republic]] history specialist from the [[Obroan Institute for Archaeology|Obroan Institute]]. Throughout the debriefing, Motti, largely due to his staunch disbelief on anything supernatural, frequently interrupted the meeting with cutting remarks on Bowen's report on the discoveries relating to [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] and the [[Rakatan revolt]] against them, causing Kurumenga to frequently reign in on him. One of his sarcastic remarks, an inference that Bowen's expertise was in [[holothriller]]s in response to the Rakatan's involvement in the conflict, was reversed when Bowen used the analogy of the villain in a holothriller not being confirmed dead to an audience even if stated unless they showed the body in order to infer the possibility that the Celestials may have survived.<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>

By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Motti was serving aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], the Empire's new [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] being constructed above [[Despayre]]. He was second-in-command alongside General [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]], below only Grand Moff Tarkin,<ref name="ds" /> a relative of Motti's through [[Thalassa Tarkin|marriage]].<ref name="praji" /> Tarkin appointed Motti for his ruthless views.<ref name="Author's Cut 11" /> The three were considered a triumvirate, with Motti representing the Imperial Navy and Tagge the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]],<ref name="dstech">''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''</ref> although Motti and Tagge had a rivalry and would openly doubt the other's competence,<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> with frequent and vociferous arguments which included Motti mocking Tagge's devotion to the Navy's starfleet.<ref name="Author's Cut 11" /> The admiral had been one of the strongest supporters of the Death Star project,<ref name="gg1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref> and felt that it was him, not Tarkin, who ran the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station's]] daily operations. He had attempted at least once to subtly convince Tarkin that whoever was in control of the Death Star held sway over the entire [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Though Palpatine, ruling from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], was the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], Motti was convinced that if Tarkin attempted to seize power by using the Death Star, he would be successful. Then, if something were to "accidentally" happen to Emperor Tarkin, his trusted assistant Motti would rise to power. Thus, Motti pretended to be loyal to the Grand Moff, all the while learning the ins and outs of the superweapon and gaining the loyalties of other key officers aboard the Death Star. During this time, he also commanded the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer [[Steel Talon/Legends|''Steel Talon'']], which was part of the fleet guarding the Death Star above Despayre.<ref name="ds" />

[[File:DSI-HDapproach.png|thumb|right|180px|The Death Star]]
As Tarkin was traveling to the Death Star from his [[Homeworld/Legends|home planet]] of [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] aboard a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by his [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]], the ship was [[Liberation of Gial Ackbar|ambushed]] by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wings]] that had been contacted by Ackbar, who sought freedom from his master. However, before the Y-wings could destroy the [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] that Tarkin had attempted to flee in, Motti's [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] jumped out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], as Motti had taken it upon himself to escort Tarkin against the Grand Moff's wishes. Thanks to the admiral, Tarkin was saved, and the Rebel Y-wings forced to flee.<ref name="darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref>

Back above Despayre, with the Death Star nearing completion, Motti met with Jaim Helaw aboard the ''[[Undauntable]]''. The two spoke about the Death Star, with Motti expressing his confidence in the battlestation, professing his belief that it would be invincible when completed. However, Helaw did not share his viewpoint, telling him the story of [[Kan Pojo]], a former Republic [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] and expert marksman. On a mission to the [[Vergesso Asteroids/Legends|Vergesso Asteroids]] to defeat a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] gang around [[35 BBY/Legends|35 BBY]], Pojo's [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] malfunctioned when he was in the act of shooting at a pirate charging him. Before the marksman could pull his other gun, the pirate was on him, [[Death/Legends|killing]] Pojo with a crude [[Knife/Legends|knife]]. When Motti stated that the Death Star was no mere blaster, Helaw responded that the more complex a weapon was, the more likely it was to have flaws. As he traveled back to the Death Star alone aboard his ship a short time later, Motti found himself wondering about Helaw's point. He decided that unlikely as an accident was, he would soon order a detailed examination of the [[Space station/Legends|station's]] superstructure.<ref name="ds" />

===Rebel interference===
{{Quote|Until this battle station is fully operational we are vulnerable. The Rebel Alliance is too well equipped. They're more dangerous than you realize.''"<br />"''Dangerous to your starfleet, Commander, not to this battle station!|Tagge and Motti|<ref name="anh" />}}
[[File:ImpStarDestroyer-SWI125.jpg|thumb|left|220px|The ''Undauntable'' was an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]]
While Motti was pondering this on the way back to the space station, the ''Undauntable'' suddenly exploded. Once the admiral landed in one of the Death Star's [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]], he met with Tarkin, who began questioning him. Motti explained that he had played no part in the ship's destruction, and that an officer of Jaim Helaw's stature would not be responsible for an accident of such large-scale. Therefore, he felt it had to be sabotage, a view the Grand Moff shared. However, fearing a visit from [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, the Emperor's lackey, Tarkin proposed that they simply record the incident as an accident while surreptitiously investigating the true cause. Though he hated to see such a stain on Jaim Helaw's record, Motti agreed, fully aware that it was best for him too without Darth Vader interfering and possibly slowing construction of the station.<ref name="ds" />

Several weeks after the ''Undauntable''{{'s}} explosion, the Rebel Alliance launched an [[Attack on the first Death Star|attack]] on the nearly completed Death Star above Despayre. It was there that the men aboard were given the first chance to test the massive [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]]. The [[Laser/Legends|laser]] easily destroyed a Rebel [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]], leaving the Rebel [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]] without a supporting [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]]. The X-wings were then wiped out by Imperial pilots, giving the Imperials total victory in the brief skirmish. Following the battle, Tarkin decided to move the battlestation to the other side of Despayre to prevent further attacks by the Rebellion.<ref name="ds" />

Not long after the battle, Tarkin decided to test the superlaser and move the station from the [[Horuz system/Legends|system]], planning to destroy Despayre as well. Motti had his doubts, and voiced them; namely, fear of political repercussion. However, as Despayre was simply a penal planet for some of the Empire's worst criminals, Tarkin was sure that no fallout would ensue. Ultimately, he was the one in command of the battlestation, and went ahead with the test. The superlaser easily [[Destruction of Despayre|destroyed]] Despayre.<ref name="ds" />

At some point during this time, Motti wrote a chapter dedicated to the Imperial Navy, which ended up included in the official field manual for the Imperial Military, ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''.<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

===Darth Vader===
{{Quote|I find your lack of faith disturbing.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] on Admiral's Motti's views|audio=LackOfFaith.flac|<ref name="anh" />}}
Following the destruction of Despayre, the Rebel Alliance managed to [[Battle of Toprawa|obtain]] a copy of the [[Death Star plans/Legends|technical readouts]] of the Death Star. The [[Tantive IV/Legends|Rebel corvette]] carrying the stolen plans was [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|captured]] by Darth Vader, but the plans themselves eluded the Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord]]. Several top Imperial officials serving aboard the Death Star became aware of the stolen plans, and Motti's sources informed him that Vader had taken [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] captive due to suspected participation in the rebels' mission. Motti was unworried by either Vader's move or the prospect of the plans to the Death Star falling into the rebels' hands, and shared these views with General Tagge during a meeting of top Imperial officials in the [[Death Star conference room/Legends|Death Star conference room]].<ref name="radio drama">[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]]</ref>

Motti further argued with General Tagge over the effectiveness of the Death Star and the threat of the Rebellion in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Tagge felt that the Rebel Alliance posed a threat to the battlestation, whereas Motti was confident that the superweapon was invincible. Tagge also feared that the growing Rebel movement would gain sympathy in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. However, the two were interrupted by Tarkin, who informed the officers present that the Senate had been [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|dissolved]] by Emperor Palpatine. Though Tagge was concerned as to how the Emperor expected to maintain control without the Senate, Tarkin revealed that the [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]], [[Governor/Legends|governors]] appointed by Palpatine, would now have direct control over [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], and the planets would not dare step out of line due to fear of the Death Star. However, Tagge continued to insist that the Rebellion was dangerous, especially if they had obtained a copy of the Death Star plans, as many Imperials feared following the Battle of Tatooine. Though Darth Vader&mdash;who had recently arrived to interrogate Leia Organa&mdash;admitted that the plans were in the hands of the Rebellion, he proclaimed that soon the Empire would have them.<ref name="anh" />

[[File:I_find_your_lack_of_faith_disturbing.png|thumb|right|300px|Vader Force chokes Motti for his lack of faith.]]
Motti then boasted of the Death Star's power, claiming that it was the preeminent power in the galaxy. However, Vader rebutted this claim, warning Motti not to underestimate the power of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Motti mocked Vader, insulting his devotion to the Force, alleging that it had not helped him recover the stolen Death Star plans or locate the Rebels' [[Great Temple/Legends|hidden base]]. In response, Vader simply [[Telekinesis/Legends#Choking powers|Force choked]] him, relenting only when ordered to do so by Tarkin.<ref name="anh" /> Motti, who had previously doubted both Vader and the power of the Force, was frightened and shocked by this display. The admiral knew that Vader would have killed him without remorse had Tarkin not stopped him, a realization that shook him greatly.<ref name="ds" /> He also realized how futile the Death Star would be against the Sith if they could kill him with a simple gesture, and resolved to be more respectful towards Vader in the future.

Soon afterward, it was reported to Motti that the Death Star was at last completely operational. He personally relayed the news to Tarkin, repeating and placing great emphasis on his belief that Tarkin had in his hands both great power and direct control over the entire galaxy. When Tarkin pointed out that they both served the Emperor, Motti stated that the Emperor was far away, and that Tarkin himself commanded the Death Star. Darth Vader then entered the room, and Tarkin advised Motti to check his ambition. The Dark Lord had been unable to force the location of the Rebel Alliance's secret base or the Death Star plans from Organa, and as such, Tarkin decided to play his trump card by threatening a third party.<ref name="radio drama" />

Tarkin ordered Motti to take the Death Star to Organa's home planet of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]],<ref name="radio drama" /> and with her alongside him, Motti and Vader in the Death Star's control room, threatened to destroy the planet if she did not reveal the location of the Alliance's base. Her resolve crumbling at the thought of her home planet and people being reduced to atoms, Organa informed them that the base was on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]. Tarkin then ordered the Death Star's superlaser to fire when ready, shocking the princess. He felt that this would be a demonstration that would terrify the rest of the galaxy; since Alderaan was admired throughout the galaxy and a prominent voice, its destruction would keep dissidents in line for fear that they would suffer the same fate. Motti gave the order to superlaser control, and then the battlestation fired, [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destroying]] Alderaan which was observed by the unremorseful Tarkin and Motti.<ref name="ds" />

A short time later, Imperial ships reached Dantooine, and discovered that while there was a Rebel base there, it had been abandoned a long time ago&mdash;meaning that Organa had lied.<ref name="anh" /> Motti reported this news to Tarkin, who in turn ordered Motti to have her terminated.<ref name="radio drama" /> However, a group of Rebels managed to make it aboard the Death Star, and succeeded in freeing Organa from her [[Detention Block AA-23/Legends|cell]]. They then fled in their ship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] had placed a [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking device]] aboard the starship earlier, however,<ref name="anh" /> and Motti reported to Tarkin that the device was transmitting a clear signal. Tarkin ordered him to follow the ship and to place all station personnel on standby alert;<ref name="radio drama" /> the Empire was able to track the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] to the rebel base on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], a [[Moon/Legends|moon]] located in the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="anh" />

===Showdown at Yavin===
{{Quote|They've fired proton torpedoes down an auxiliary heat shaft. Incoming! Incoming! The reactor will blow!|Motti's last words|<ref name="ds" />}}
The Death Star jumped to hyperspace, arriving in the Yavin system, where the Rebel Alliance was preparing an [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|attack]]. The Alliance's defense of its base consisted of thirty [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], catching the Imperials off-guard, as Tarkin had expected to be opposed by several [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]].<ref name="ds" /> Confident in the ability of the Death Star's [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] and other anti-starfighter defenses to repel the Alliance's fighters, he withheld from launching Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighters]].<ref name="anh" /> As the Death Star [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]], waiting to clear the planet before it could strike at the moon, Motti placed the entire station on full alert status. As he stood alone with Tarkin, he congratulated the Grand Moff on his impending destruction of the Rebellion, again emphasizing that it was Tarkin, and not the Emperor, who held the ultimate power in the galaxy. When Tarkin insisted he cease the vague hints and speak freely, Motti suggested that Tarkin's command of the Death Star could elevate him to a position that equaled the Emperor's in power. He would serve as Tarkin's right hand, and would even take steps to eliminate Vader if it proved necessary. Tarkin considered his offer, but suggested that they discuss it further after eradicating the rebels.<ref name="radio drama" />

When several X-wing fighters proved adept at evading the station's defenses, Vader manned his [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|personal TIE fighter]] and attacked them. He began picking off the surviving fighters one by one,<ref name="anh" /> but Tarkin nevertheless began to worry that the rebel attack posed a danger. He ordered Motti to prepare his personal escape shuttle, but Motti was adamant that he not appear ready to relinquish his power by abandoning the Death Star. Tarkin conceded, and adopted a more confident demeanor.<ref name="radio drama" /> However, the Alliance was aware of a flaw in the Death Star&mdash;a small, uncovered [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] leading directly to the station's [[Reactor/Legends|main reactor]]. Against all odds, and much to Tarkin's surprise, a Rebel X-wing piloted by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] succeeded in flying through the trench where the exhaust port was located, and successfully fired a pair of [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into the shaft, causing the Death Star to explode,<ref name="anh" /> instantly killing Motti,<ref name="ds" /> and all those on board.<ref name="anh" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Any attack made by the Rebels against this station would be a useless gesture, no matter what technical data they've obtained. This station is now the ultimate power in the universe! I suggest we use it.|Motti|<ref name="anh" />}}
[[File:Motti2.png|thumb|left|220px|Conan Antonio Motti]]
As a teenager during the Clone Wars, Motti was thrilled by the exploits of the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]], with reserved contempt for both the Republic [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucrats]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], whom he felt hamstrung the [[Outland Regions]] Security Force and incompetently prosecuted the Clone Wars from the distant [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. Motti cheered when he heard of the Jedi's [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|elimination]] as traitors of the Republic, and was moved by Palpatine's declaration that the new order would get rid of the corruption and vacillation of previous eras. As Motti saw the Empire took the galactic stage at a time of unprecedented promise, he believed in the New Order's goals being spread across the galaxy and planets could not adapt should be eliminated, with other worlds considering the consequences. Within the Navy, he held the greatest contempt for veterans of the Republic's [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]] or [[Planetary Security Forces]], as he believed their loyalty was to their own service and not the Empire, and he disagreed with what he considered their outdated ideas of military power.<ref name="Author's Cut 11" />

Motti was a deeply ambitious man, a fact acknowledged by Tarkin. The Grand Moff held the opinion that once the Rebels were destroyed, Motti would receive a promotion to Moff. Indeed, the admiral was very ambitious, and though he seemed loyal to Emperor Palpatine, in truth Motti harbored dreams of becoming Emperor himself.<ref name="ds" /> He attempted to convert Tarkin to his cause, trying to convince the Grand Moff that whoever controlled the Death Star could control the galaxy. Motti hoped that Tarkin would soon listen to him, and use the Death Star to seize power from Palpatine.<ref name="ds" /><ref name="radio drama" /> If Tarkin did overthrow Palpatine, the admiral would then cause Tarkin's death in a subtle way, allowing him to ultimately become Emperor.<ref name="ds" /> He also believed Darth Vader had similar ideas, with Vader's first act under Emperor Tarkin would be to eliminate his rivals,<ref name="Author's Cut 11" /> and was additionally prepared to arrange for Vader's death if it proved necessary.<ref name="radio drama" /> However, he never received this chance, as the Death Star was destroyed by the Rebel Alliance shortly after its completion.<ref name="ds" />

Motti believed in the infallibility of the Death Star, feeling that any attack made by the rebellion against the station would be a useless gesture doomed to fail.<ref name="anh" /><ref name="radio drama" /> So strong was his belief in the Death Star that he was its greatest champion, and told any who would listen that it was the missing piece of his long-held military philosophy, in which, while the Navy normally commanded space and protected the Army during [[Ground warfare/Legends|ground assaults]], the Death Star's threat would free the Army to act, leaving the Navy's endless parade of battleships superfluous.<ref name="Author's Cut 11" /> During the Battle of Yavin, his faith in the battle station and his quest for power saw him dissuade a worried Tarkin from preparing an escape shuttle. Motti believed that in order to seize power, Tarkin could never abandon the Death Star; he further dismissed the rebel attack as nothing to be concerned about. Tarkin heeded his advice, which ultimately led to both of their deaths.<ref name="radio drama" /> Admiral Motti was a firm believer in the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]], which stated that the threat of force was sufficient enough to prevent rebellions, and that fear was necessary to keep dissidents in line. Ultimately, this belief was flawed, as the Destruction of Alderaan did not cause other planets to cower in fear, but instead to rise up in anger and challenge the Empire&mdash;which led to the Death Star's destruction and Motti's death.<ref name="ds" /> He, like Tarkin, also despised the Imperial Navy's generationals for their belief in stability and order, as they believed that they were "ancient values."<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

Motti pretended to be loyal to Tarkin, though in truth it was in an act, designed to fool the Grand Moff and ensure that he trusted Motti, so that if the admiral ever decided to betray him, Tarkin would be caught unaware. To further this facade, Motti pretended to be sympathetic towards Tarkin when his mistress, Admiral [[Natasi Daala]], was injured in the Attack on the first Death Star. He was even prepared to feign sadness in the event that Daala died, hoping to curry favor with the Grand Moff. Motti was also aware that if he did not act appropriately disheartened, Tarkin would be greatly insulted, and the admiral knew that it was not wise to offend Tarkin. Motti considered Tarkin's affection for Daala a weakness, and was prepared to one day exploit that.<ref name="ds" />

Motti felt that women were inferior to men, believing that Daala did not deserve her rank of admiral, and that she would not have achieved it if Tarkin had not taken favor to her. He thought that Leia Organa had a strong spirit due to her refusing to give up the location of the Rebel base, and because she criticized and insulted Tarkin even when he threatened to execute her. Motti was impressed with her determination to not surrender, believing that this fortitude was especially stunning in a woman.<ref name="ds" />

The Admiral was also a strong-minded man, though not without arrogance, overly-confident in himself and the Death Star.<ref name="ds" /> He was aware of how quickly he had risen through the Imperial ranks, and that he had jumped ahead of a number of more experienced officers to his position as head of Navy Operations aboard the Death Star. This was reflected in his attitude, as he frequently wore a smug look and took extra pride in ensuring that his uniform was even neater than required by Imperial standards.<ref name="dstech" /> He also prided himself on being physically fit, and regularly exercised, hoping to never become a fat, lazy officer like so many others. Motti felt that being physically stronger than others was a symbol of power, and would earn him additional respect.<ref name="ds" /> He constantly belittled the Rebel Alliance, believing them to be only a nagging pain rather than a serious threat. He was proven wrong when the fledgling Alliance managed to infiltrate the defenses and destroy the Death Star.

Though he very highly valued his political and tactical skills, Motti was considered somewhat of an overrated leader by many, who felt that his only real skill lay in loyalty to Palpatine's Empire, and that he had padded his record.<ref name="dstech" /> In fact, Motti had little actual command experience, and embellished his reports, making himself appear more capable than he was in reality. It was thanks mainly to his many connections that he rose through the ranks as rapidly as he did, although he believed strongly in his own abilities.<ref name="ff" />

Admiral Motti questioned the Force, and disliked Vader, feeling that he used archaic methods,<ref name="ds" /> and, though never opposing the Dark Lord, would take every opportunity to belittle him in front of Tarkin,<ref name="Author's Cut 11" /> such as when he heavily criticized Vader for his failure to wrest the location of the Rebel base from Princess Leia Organa. For this criticism, Vader Force-choked him. Following this, Motti was mollified, and began to develop a fear of Vader and his mysterious [[Force power/Legends|powers]]. The admiral knew that had Tarkin not interfered, Vader would have killed him, a deeply sobering thought to him. Though he did not consider himself cowardly, Motti was frightened by Vader, aware that controlling a planet-destroying superweapon meant nothing if he could be simply killed by a gesture. Following this, Motti planned to eliminate Vader somehow, although he was aware that such an act would have to be done very carefully.<ref name="ds" />

Aside from his staunch disbelief in the Force, Motti also was a staunch disbeliever in any aspects of the supernatural to the extent that he was fully prepared to mock anyone who suggested the possibility of supernatural influences in the galaxy. This was best demonstrated during a debriefing on Coruscant in 1 BBY, where he frequently criticized and mocked Dr. Bowen to such an extent that one of his fellow Imperial Generals, Arhul Kurumenga, frequently had to reign in on him for interrupting the debriefing.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Tarkin was cognizant of Motti's fear and hatred of Vader and his Force, and believed that if Motti did not do a better job of keeping his opinions to himself, he would not live much longer in Palpatine's Empire. The admiral doubted the Force, even mocking Vader's confidence in it until Vader Force-choked him as a warning. He preferred to place his confidence in technology, and he remained extremely certain of the Death Star's invulnerability throughout his life.<ref name="dstech" />

At one time, Vader [[Force empathy/Legends|detected]] Motti's silent, boiling rage and jealousy, which were mostly directed towards him. The Sith Lord came to believe that had the Admiral been born [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], he would have been of invaluable use.<ref name="ds" />

Motti had fair skin and [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]].<ref name="anh" /> He stood at a height of 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="ff" />

==Equipment==
Admiral Motti wore the standard-issue [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|Imperial officer's uniform]].<ref name="anh" /> His equipment included an [[E-11 blaster pistol]],<ref name="hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Saga Collection|pack=Death Star Briefing|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tscdeathstarbriefing.asp}}</ref> along with a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] and a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]].<ref name="GG12E">[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'', Second Edition]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Portrayal===
{{Quote|Oh yes. I was fortunate I was sent a complete script! A lot of people weren't sent complete scripts of the first film, they were sent a few pages. I'd actually read it and thought 'God, this is just so hard to get through!' It was 155 pages. It was so detailed with the descriptions and the dialogue was not very good. If you got through the script, it was such a good story that I thought 'OK, this could work.' I thought 'I know they could do this,' because they wouldn't make it if they couldn't do the special effects.|Richard LeParmentier, commenting on his ''A New Hope'' script|<ref name="Insider 96">{{InsiderCite|96|The Men Who Built the Empire}}</ref>}}
[[File:Richard_LeParmentier.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Motti was portrayed by American actor Richard LeParmentier]]
Motti first appeared in the film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], released in [[1977]]. He was played by [[Richard LeParmentier]], who was credited as "General Motti."<ref name="anh" /> Motti was originally slated to be an Admiral, but when LeParmentier proved to be too tall for the Admiral's uniform that was to be his costume, he was fitted in a General's uniform and the character's rank was changed. The ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] later solidified his rank as Admiral despite the costume discrepancy.<ref name="Motti Dearest">{{InsiderCite|40|In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Richard LeParmentier}}</ref>

LeParmentier originally auditioned for the role of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], one of ''Star Wars''{{'s}} leading characters, and was offered the role of a customs officer who tried to stop Solo from leaving the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]. He turned down the role, which was ultimately cut from the film, but was invited back to read for the part of Motti.<ref name="Motti Dearest" /> LeParmentier was one of the few non-English actors cast as Imperial officers, and as such is one of the only Imperial officers in the [[original trilogy]] to speak without an English accent.<ref name="anh" /><ref name="esb">{{Film|V}}</ref><ref name="rotj">{{Film|VI}}</ref> In order to make the scene where Motti is Force-choked by Darth Vader look convincing, LeParmentier spent days practicing choking in his dressing room until he was able to induce and control spasms in his neck.<ref name="Motti Dearest" />

Richard LeParmentier stated that he was pleased to be remembered as Motti, and that he considers it an honor to have been part of ''Star Wars''.<ref name="actor">{{WebCite|url=http://www.admiralmotti.co.uk|text=Admiral Motti|archivedate=20161022100837}}</ref> He was proud of the fact that Vader's choking of Motti was the first point in the ''Star Wars'' saga that fans saw the power of the Force at work, although he had no idea at the time that the film would be as successful as it ultimately was. LeParmentier greatly enjoyed his time working on ''Star Wars'', and cited the only inconvenience that he faced on set as his character's boots, which caused him a considerable amount of foot perspiration. Between shots, crewmembers would take the boots of the Imperial officers off and air-dry their feet.<ref name="Motti Dearest" />

While playing the role of Motti, LeParmentier saw his character as a trigger-happy military type who was aching to demonstrate the power of the Death Star and was resentful of anyone who disagreed with that idea. He played Motti as a smug and sanctimonious character, believing that the contrast with [[Don Henderson]]'s calm and reasonable portrayal of Tagge was necessary to prompt Vader to use the Force on him.<ref name="Motti Dearest" /> LeParmentier was producing an animated fan film called ''Motti Now'', in which Motti survives the Battle of Yavin and abandons the Empire.<ref name="actor" />

===Motti in other related media===
[[File:Motti-MSW1.jpg|thumb|left|140px|Motti appeared as a bald, older man in the Marvel comic book adaptation]]
Early scripts of ''A New Hope'' shuffled the names of Admiral Motti and General Tagge. He is absent from the Death Star meeting scene in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization of ''A New Hope'']], and instead it is General Tagge who is the victim of Vader's telekinetic strangulation, while Motti himself is replaced by a new Imperial officer named [[Hurst Romodi/Legends|Romodi]]. Motti does appear later on in the novel, proving that he and Romodi are different characters. [[Leland Chee]], the keeper of the ''Star Wars'' [[Holocron continuity database]], nevertheless confirmed that Romodi is a senator and a different character than Motti.<ref name="chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=1170#16176459|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2007-01-15|time=10:06 AM}}</ref> In the [[1978]] book ''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]'', Tagge was the one who said Motti's dialogue and spoke out against Vader.<ref name="SWS">''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]''</ref>

Motti's role was greatly expanded in the [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama of ''Star Wars'']], in which he attempts to conspire with Tarkin to eliminate Vader and assume complete control of the Empire. In the radio drama, [[David Clennon]] provided Motti's voice.<ref name="radio drama" /> In [[Star Wars (1977) 2|''Star Wars'' (1977) 2]], an issue of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] adaptation of ''Star Wars'', Motti is shown at first with white hair, and later with blond hair.

[[Jason Fry]], the author of [[2012]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', originally planned to include Motti in the book's prologue. Motti, Imperial [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]], an unnamed General representing the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]], and Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]] were slated to discuss various mysterious events within the Galaxy, with Motti doubting Bowen's assertion that they were the result of ancient [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] technology. The prologue was ultimately cut and replaced with [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Osvald Teshik]]'s account of the [[Battle of Andalia]]. The decision came from [[Del Rey]] editor [[Erich Schoeneweiss]], who felt that an account of a battle from a first-hand witness would better hook the reader. Fry begrudgingly agreed.<ref name="JLT1">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/20843004826/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-1|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 1}}</ref> Fry also planned to write a war portrait of Motti in the book as well, to show the differing views of the younger and older Imperial officers regarding the Empire. However, as he felt too much of it was a rehash of content in ''The Essential Atlas'', and the piece was too short with that material cut, he ended up cutting that section of the book as well.<ref name="Author's Cut 11" />

===Naming origins===
{{Quote|See, because Lucas is the supreme creator of the Star Wars universe, ''when he says something it becomes real''. Oh yeah. I think you hear what I'm saying, party people: ''There is now officially a Star Wars character named after Conan!! HOW AWECELLET IS THAT?!'' The Star Wars wiki Wookieepedia has already incorporated the change into the Star Wars Mythology! Man! This week couldn't get any better!|Conan O'Brien's NBC blog|<ref name="blog">{{WebCite|url=https://blog.nbc.com/latenight/2007/05/breaking_hearts_and_making_far.php|text=Conan O'Brien's NBC.com blog|date=2008-05-02|work=NBC|archivedate=20080303214713}}</ref>}}
Motti was one of the last Imperial characters from the [[original trilogy]] to receive a full name. [[Michael Reaves]] and [[Steve Perry]] intended to finally give the character a first name with their [[2007]] novel [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']], and had already chosen the name "Zi"&mdash;used in the as-yet unpublished novel&mdash;when George Lucas created his own name for the character while being interviewed on [[Wikipedia:Late Night with Conan O'Brien|''Late Night with Conan O'Brien'']]. Following this, the writers were forced to change the name before printing, although one instance of "Zi" remains in the novel. Motti's full name was given by Lucas on the [[May 1]], [[2007]] episode of ''Late Night with Conan O'Brien'', during which Lucas was challenged to a trivia question by a fan&mdash;''O'Brien'' Associate Producer Jordan Schlanski&mdash;as to the name of the Imperial officer who Darth Vader Force-chokes in ''A New Hope''. Lucas jokingly replied "Conan Antonio Motti." Although the character had previously been known only as "Motti," Lucas's statement finally gave a full name to this character. On the day after the episode aired, ''Late Night'' posted a blog entry on the NBC website about their surprise at the [[Special:Diff/1315629|quick response]] of [[Wookieepedia]], a fan-made online ''Star Wars'' Encyclopedia, in adopting the new name for the character, as well as their appreciation for Lucas in naming a ''Star Wars'' character after O'Brien.<ref name="blog" />

[[File:Coco.jpg|thumb|right|190px|Conan O'Brien, Motti's namesake]]
When asked at [[Celebration IV]] to confirm the [[canon]] status of Motti's first name, Leland Chee said that "It'll be revealed eventually."<ref name="continuity">[[Forum:CIV Continuity Questions|Continuity Q & A at Celebration IV]]</ref> The name was finally confirmed when [[Sue Rostoni]], executive editor of [[Lucas Licensing]], posted the ''dramatis personae'' for ''Death Star'' on the [[StarWars.com]] message boards.<ref name="rostoni">{{SWBoards|url=message.jspa?messageID=16770795#16770795|thread=Books, Comics, & Television VIPs|user=[[Sue Rostoni]]|date=2007-07-05|time=1:47 PM|nobackup=1}}</ref>
